title: Preemptible Capacity Crediting Guidelines
author: Marco Nguyen
body:
Overview
--------

Purpose: This playbook defines how Redwood will credit customers for use of preemptible (interruptible) capacity across Dedicated and Private deployments. It standardizes the crediting model, reconciliation events, edge cases, and API hooks required for automation. The target audience is billing/product managers, finance, SRE leads, and platform engineers implementing the crediting logic.

Summary: When a request is served on preemptible capacity and is either curtailed because of preemption or migrated to non-preemptible capacity with degraded fidelity, customers will receive a credit composed of: (1) token-cost refund component, (2) preemption-finesse uplift (for degraded fidelity or increased latency), and (3) a throughput-availability credit. This doc defines triggers, formulas, and examples.

Scope
-----

Included:
- Preemptible GPU capacity attached to Dedicated pools and Private on-prem cluster pools managed by Redwood.
- Hosted fallback to compatible non-preemptible variant when preemptible capacity unavailable.
- Customer-visible crediting on invoices and console.

Excluded:
- Short-lived network blips unrelated to capacity preemption (handled by SRE incident credits).
- Credits for model quality regressions (handled by Optimize product guardrails).

Definitions
-----------

- Preemptible capacity: compute units that may be reclaimed by the node scheduler within 120s notice or less and are priced lower than reserved capacity.
- Creditable-event: a billing event where customer workload experienced either (A) a preemption that led to request interruption, or (B) an automated fallback that materially reduced fidelity or latency beyond SLO thresholds.
- Token-cost refund: proportional refund of the per-token charge for the affected request(s).
- Finesse uplift: a flat-rate adjustment to reflect customer impact for degraded fidelity or >95th latency percentile degradation.
- Availability credit: a time-proportional credit applied when preemptible pool availability falls below target thresholds for the customer’s committed reservation.

Goals and Constraints
---------------------

Goals:
- Predictable and auditable crediting rules to reduce disputes.
- Incentivize customers to adopt preemptible capacity while preserving SLA clarity for reserved tiers.
- Automation-first: everything mapped to events and telemetry to enable self-service credits.

Constraints:
- Credits must be reconciled within 30 days of event for monthly billing cycles.
- Credits cannot exceed total token spend for affected requests.
- Manual adjustments require Finance approval if >$10k per customer per month.

Crediting Model
---------------

1) Trigger types and detection logic:
   a) Preemption-interrupt: detected when node-level lifecycle event (NODE_PREEMPTED) is correlated with active request ID and request terminated before final token emission.
   b) Fallback-degraded: detected when request was auto-routed to fallback variant and fidelity downgrade flag or latency_slo_breach is true.
   c) Pool-unavailability: detected when customer's dedicated preemptible pool available_capacity < target_floor for >5 minutes.

2) Credit components (formula descriptions):
   - Token-cost refund = min(charged_tokens_for_request, tokens_emitted) * per_token_rate * refundable_fraction
   - Refundable_fraction = 1.0 for interruptions before final token; 0.50 for degraded-fidelity fallback where partial response returned.
   - Finesse uplift = if latency_slo_breach then flat_rate_usd_per_event else 0; flat_rate_usd_per_event = $0.10 by default for hosted API, adjustable per-customer contract.
   - Availability credit = (committed_monthly_reserved_cost * downtime_minutes / total_month_minutes) * availability_weight

3) Example calculation (text table):

| Scenario | Charged tokens | Tokens returned | per_token_rate | refundable_fraction | Token refund | Finesse uplift | Availability credit | Total credit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Interrupted request | 120 | 30 | $0.0006 | 1.0 | $0.018 | $0.00 | $0.00 | $0.018 |
| Fallback degraded | 300 | 300 | $0.0006 | 0.5 | $0.09 | $0.10 | $0.00 | $0.19 |

Event lifecycle and reconciliation
----------------------------------

1. Detection: SRE telemetry emits an event with request_id, customer_id, node_id, event_type, timestamp.
2. Classification: Billing pipeline joins event with request trace to classify as creditable-event.
3. Pre-approval window: System computes provisional credit within 24h and posts to customer console as "Pending credit".
4. Reconciliation: After 30-day lookback or when final charges settle, credits are posted to invoice as line-items with tags: PREEMPT_REFUND, FINESSE_UPLIFT, AVAILABILITY_CREDIT.
5. Dispute handling: Customers can open ticket; automated disputes are available for credits < $500 via the console. Larger disputes route to Finance for manual review.

APIs and Implementations
-----------------------

- Event schema (example JSON payload):

{
  "event_type": "NODE_PREEMPTED",
  "request_id": "req_1234",
  "customer_id": "cust_5678",
  "node_id": "node-az1-17",
  "timestamp": "2026-07-18T12:05:33Z",
  "tokens_emitted": 30,
  "tokens_charged": 120
}

- Billing query (SQL pseudocode) to compute provisional credits per customer per day:

-- join telemetry_events -> requests -> invoices
SELECT customer_id, SUM(token_refund + finesse + availability_credit) as provisional_credit
FROM credit_calculations WHERE event_date = CURRENT_DATE GROUP BY customer_id;

- Console representation: "Credits > Pending" tab with filters (date-range, event-type, min-amount). Each credit line includes supporting trace link and node metadata.

Billing UX and Invoice line items
--------------------------------

- Line item codes: PREEMPT_REFUND, PREEMPT_FINESSE, PREEMPT_AVAILABILITY.
- Invoice description sample: "Preemptible capacity refund (NODE_PREEMPTED) 2026-07-18 — credits applied to usage".
- Credits will reduce next invoice by default; customers on custom billing cycles may request immediate payout via support.

Edge cases and policy decisions
-------------------------------

- If a request is retried and final successful emission occurs on non-preemptible capacity within the platform’s fallback window (120s), only the earliest interrupted request is eligible for token-cost refund. Retries that complete incur normal charges.
- When the same request is partially emitted across preemptible and non-preemptible nodes, token refund is proportional to tokens emitted on the preempted node.
- Rate-limited customers: credits must not be used to bypass quota enforcement; credits affect only billing amounts, not quota counters.

Operational runbook (SRE <-> Billing integration)
--------------------------------------------------

1. SRE: emit NODE_PREEMPTED and FALLBACK_ROUTE events with standardized tags.
2. Platform-billing: subscribe to telemetry stream and run classification job every 10 minutes.
3. Finance: run daily reconcile to surface high-value provisional credits (> $1k) and approve auto-apply thresholds.
4. Support: guide disputes, escalate when >$10k.

Rollout plan
------------

Phase 0 — Design signoff (2 weeks): document review, schema approval, telemetry mapping.
Phase 1 — Pilot (1 month): Pilot with 3 large tenants on Dedicated preemptible pools. Credits are preview-only in console.
Phase 2 — Auto-apply (1 month): Enable auto-apply for provisional credits <= $500. Monitor dispute rate.
Phase 3 — General availability (1 week): Public docs, product announcement, invoices include credits by default.

Monitoring and SLOs
-------------------

- Detection accuracy: >= 99.5% of NODE_PREEMPTED events must map to request traces for pilot tenants.
- Credit latency: provisional credit appears in console within 24h for 95% of events.
- Reconciliation SLA: final credit posted on invoice within 30 days for 99% of events.

Metrics to track:
- daily_credit_volume_usd, daily_credit_count, avg_credit_latency_seconds, disputes_count, disputed_value_usd

Telemetry and data retention
---------------------------

- Keep event-level telemetry for 90 days in hot storage for reconciliation and 2 years in cold archive per Finance policy.
- Redact PII from traces; only store customer_id and request_id references.

Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
-------------------------------

Q: Will credits affect my SLA?
A: Credits are billing adjustments and do not change SLA entitlements. Customers with SLO-backed contracts may receive additional remedies as contractually required.

Q: Can I opt-out of preemptible credits?
A: No — credit policy applies to all customers using preemptible pools. Customers may opt for non-preemptible reserved capacity instead.

Q: How are credits shown in the console?
A: Each pending credit includes supporting traces and a short explanation. Final credits appear as invoice line items with links to the original events.

Appendix A — Example dispute workflow
------------------------------------

1. Customer opens dispute from console and selects affected credit line.
2. Support triages with automated data extract (trace + node lifecycle).
3. If automated evidence insufficient, escalate to Finance with supporting artifacts.
4. Resolution timeline: target 5 business days for credits < $1k, 15 business days for larger cases.

Appendix B — Configurable knobs per customer
--------------------------------------------

- refundable_fraction_override (contract level)
- finesse_flat_rate_override
- auto_apply_threshold_usd
